identity.title: The Dynamics of Infall and Accretion Shocks in the Outer Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: We construct synthetic observations and find that the deviations from circular Keplerian orbits are detectable in Doppler-shifted molecular spectral lines using radio interferometers such as ALMA.
We examine archival ALMA data for the class 0/I protostar L1527

question.value: Do shocks where infalling envelope gas meets the outer disk produce non-circular (elliptical) gas orbits whose Doppler signatures in line moment maps can be detected with ALMA, as tested against archival C18O data of L1527

evidence.loc: abstract
evidence.quote: We investigate the role of shocks using a theoretical and modeling framework we call the shock twist-angle Keplerian (STAK) disk, connecting the disk and infalling envelope gas via a shock using general physical principles.

claims.hypothesis: Gas passing through an envelope-disk shock follows elliptical orbits that leave an observable kinematic signature distinct from circular Keplerian rotation
claims.experiment: Built the STAK model in RadChemT and made synthetic C18O(2-1) cubes and moment maps for circular and elliptical disks at several inclinations
claims.result: Elliptical models show asymmetric, twisted moment 0 and moment 1 maps relative to the disk major axis, unlike circular models
claims.finding: The STAK disk leaves an inner twist detectable with ALMA spectral line data

evidence.loc: 7 Conclusions
evidence.quote: The resulting disk gas streamlines deviate from circular Keplerian orbits in ways detectable using spectral line data from interferometers such as ALMA.

claims.hypothesis: The STAK signature survives limited spatial resolution
claims.experiment: Convolved the 75 au disk models with Gaussian beams of 8, 25 and 75 au at i=60 and 85 deg
claims.result: Moment 0 asymmetry largely disappears at 25 and 75 au, while the moment 1 velocity asymmetry persists
claims.finding: Velocity moment maps are the better diagnostic for marginally resolved disks

evidence.loc: 7 Conclusions
evidence.quote: For disks that are only marginally spatially-resolved, the STAK signature is retained best in the velocity moment map.

claims.hypothesis: Archival ALMA C18O(2-1) data of L1527 show STAK-like asymmetries
claims.experiment: Compared by eye the Cycle 0 moment 1 map (0.96'' x 0.73'') with circular and elliptical models at 0.84'' resolution and i=85 and 95 deg
claims.result: The elliptical model at i=95 deg matches the peak red and blue positions and the inner twist best
claims.finding: Improved agreement over the circular model and a preferred inclination of 95 deg, but the match is qualitative

referee_caveats_inferred: Model-data comparison is visual with no goodness-of-fit, so the inclination preference of 95 vs 85 deg is not statistically supported
Only one archival ALMA dataset (coarse 0.84'' effective resolution) is used, so the test is weak for a thin disk of about 75 au radius
Other mechanisms (infalling envelope ballistic orbits, streamers, warps) could produce similar twists and are not excluded quantitatively
Only the C18O line is modelled and optical depth and continuum over-subtraction can mimic asymmetries
Synthetic observations are not passed through ALMA uv sampling or noise, only convolved with a Gaussian
